definitions.specifically-named-reaction-cases: Named source examples/material systems retained with exact source scope; not every named item implies every conceivable variant.
definitions.general-example-family: Representative family/conditional application; named editorial examples are not publisher-exclusive obligations.
definitions.cross-topic-equation-skill: Equation, representation or calculation skill spanning justified examples, not a new reaction count.
definitions.no-separately-prescribed-reaction: This statement concerns structures/charges/physical properties/terminology, not a separately mandated reaction.

decisions.judgement: Oxide acid/base behaviour supports classification, but no particular oxide or acid is named.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Representative basic oxide + acid; acidic oxide + base (select from studied salts/carbon-dioxide cases).
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Use supplied oxide behaviour; not every metal oxide dissolves or is basic and not every non-metal oxide is acidic. Examples are not an exhaustive oxide reaction set.

decisions.judgement: Similar outer-shell configurations explain group chemical similarities; concrete reactions belong the group-specific identities.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Representative Group1 water and halogen displacement cases cross-reference2.1–2.8C.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: No additional reaction pair is named here; do not multiply group-specific cases or equate similar chemistry with identical rates.

decisions.judgement: Explicitly covers word/balanced chemical equations with states for studied reactions AND unfamiliar reactions given suitable information.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: All source-justified studied reaction cases through cross-links; separate unfamiliar information-to-equation transfer task.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: This is the umbrella skill, not an additional named reaction or finite memorisation list. States must follow given temperature/solvent/phase; complete cross-topic audit needed before coverage claim.

decisions.judgement: Reacting masses use experimental data and balanced chemical equations; no reagent pair prescribed.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Representative supplied balanced-equation mass ratio and experimental mass analysis.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Use actual reacting/limiting amount and coefficient basis; no requirement to enumerate every numerical substitution.

decisions.judgement: Source explicitly includes metal oxides, water, and salts containing water of crystallisation, but does not name one exclusive reagent route.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Metal-oxide mass gain or oxygen loss; experimental composition of water; hydrated-salt water-loss composition.
Existing examples:2Mg(s)+O2(g)→2MgO(s); CuO(s)+H2(g)→Cu(s)+H2O; CuSO4·5H2O(s)→CuSO4(s)+5H2O.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Keep all three material classes represented. Water state depends on hot production versus cooled collection; hydrate loss requires no salt decomposition and no other mass loss. These named examples are editorial choices, not exclusive publisher reagents.

decisions.judgement: Practical permits metal-oxide formula determination by combustion OR reduction, with MgO and CuO introduced as examples.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Combustion example2Mg(s)+O2(g)→2MgO(s).
Alternative reduction exampleCuO(s)+H2(g)→Cu(s)+H2O(g), with collected water possibly(l) after cooling.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Source says OR, not mandatory performed trials of both. Mass accounting needs complete intended reaction/no product loss; Mg nitrogen side-reaction is a caveat, not another prescribed practical. School-controlled heating/reduction; no home apparatus instruction.

decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Formal atom/ion diagrams are not automatically full reactions under ambient conditions; molecular halogen electrode equations must use X2 and correct phase when applicable.

decisions.judgement: Inert-electrode experiments explicitly include molten lead(II)bromide and aqueous sodium chloride, dilute sulfuric acid and copper(II)sulfate, plus prediction skill.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: MoltenPbBr2(l)→Pb(l)+Br2(g) under hot molten-cell conditions; Pb2++2e−→Pb and2Br−→Br2+2e−.
Concentrated aqueousNaCl with inert electrodes:2NaCl(aq)+2H2O(l)→2NaOH(aq)+H2(g)+Cl2(g); cathode water reduction and chloride oxidation.
DiluteH2SO4(aq), inert electrodes: net2H2O(l)→2H2(g)+O2(g).
AqueousCuSO4, genuinely inert electrodes: copper cathode deposit and oxygen anode; net2CuSO4(aq)+2H2O(l)→2Cu(s)+O2(g)+2H2SO4(aq).
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Publisher NaCl case does not specify concentration: distinguish brine chlorine from dilute-chloride oxygen competition, not universal chlorine-only. Pb product liquid in hot cell versus solid after cooling. Cu electrodes change anode reaction; graphite can react with oxygen. Half-equations must specify aqueous or molten context. Named cases do not exhaust unfamiliar prediction skill.

decisions.judgement: Ionic electrode half-equations and oxidation/reduction classification span electrolysis cases; no extra electrolyte named.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Cross-link1.58C cathode/anode cases: Pb2+/Pb, Br−/Br2, Cu2+/Cu, H+/H2 or water/H2, water/O2 or OH−/O2, Cl−/Cl2.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Conserve atoms and charge; oxidation emits electrons, reduction consumes them. Acidic and alkaline representations must be chemically/contextually consistent; do not mix phase assumptions or count alternative forms as separate required reactions.

decisions.judgement: Aqueous electrolysis practical names a family, without an additional fixed electrolyte list.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Aqueous investigation representativeCuSO4 with suitable inert electrodes, linked to1.58C; source named aqueous acid/NaCl cases remain separately covered there.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Practical plans/observations and reaction equations are separate evidence; no obligation to claim every aqueous solution tested. Qualified graphite products, controlled DC/electrodes, separate gas identification and no performed-trial claim.

decisions.judgement: Exothermic/endothermic definitions require representative heat-transfer changes, not a named pair.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Representative neutralisation exotherm and suitable dissolving endotherm from3.2/3.8.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Dissolving can be physical solvation/dissociation rather than a new chemical reaction; initial heating does not establish endothermicity.

decisions.judgement: Source names calorimetry example types: combustion, displacement, dissolving and neutralisation, without fixing reagents.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Combustion representative fuel+O2→CO2+H2O; neutralisationHCl(aq)+NaOH(aq)→NaCl(aq)+H2O(l).
DisplacementZn(s)+CuSO4(aq)→ZnSO4(aq)+Cu(s); dissolving a suitable specified salt in water.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Represent all four method classes; selected examples do not require every fuel/salt/acid pair. Water combustion state follows stated calorimetry basis, not arbitrary(g)/(l). Dissolving needs chosen substance/dissociation and mass assumptions.

decisions.judgement: Q=mcΔT is a cross-reaction heat calculation, not another named chemical reaction.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Apply to actual selected calorimetry case.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Use measured material mass and heat capacity; distinguish sign of surroundingsQ from reactionheat.

decisions.judgement: Molar enthalpy calculated from heat and reacting amount uses a specified equation basis.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Calorimetry case per mole of stated reactant or equation extent.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Coefficient/limiting-amount basis and physical states matter; no fixed reagent list.

decisions.judgement: Energy-level diagrams represent exo/endothermic reactions without prescribing reagent identities.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: One exothermic and one endothermic supplied reaction/energy model.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Represent unchanged equation basis and products-minus-reactants sign; no added named cases.

decisions.judgement: Bond breaking/making energy directions apply across represented chemical changes.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Representative supplied bond-breaking/formation accounting.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Not a requirement to isolate every bond experimentally or introduce extra named reactions.

decisions.judgement: Bond-energy enthalpy estimation requires balanced structures and coefficients but no named equation.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Representative gas-phase reaction with supplied bond energies; existing ammonia model is editorial.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Average gas-phase model; states and stoichiometric basis explicit. Supplied examples do not make ammonia synthesis a separately prescribed named case here.

decisions.judgement: Practical investigates SOME of salts dissolving, neutralisation, displacement and combustion.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Select appropriate temperature-change practical(s) from four listed families; cross-link3.2 examples.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Preserve SOME: no mandatory four performed trials, and no new fixed salt/fuel/acid list. Authored method coverage differs from empirical execution.

decisions.judgement: Investigations span area, solution concentration, temperature and catalyst without a new fixed reaction list.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Marble/HCl for area/concentration; peroxide/solids for catalyst; approved temperature-controlled representative reaction.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Four variable demands need teaching; gas pressure is added by3.10/3.11, not an extra mandated3.9 experiment. Named reactions belong3.15/3.16; avoid duplicate required-case counts.

decisions.judgement: Effects of area/concentration/gaspressure/temperature/catalyst are a general rate family.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Use source-justified rate/catalyst examples linked3.15/3.16.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Same final yield requires same fully reacted limiting amount and matched gas conditions; no universal exact rate multiplier.

decisions.judgement: Collision theory explains area/concentration/pressure/temperature effects without a new named chemical pair.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Use source-justified rate/catalyst examples linked3.15/3.16.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Fixed-temperature compression raises reacting concentration, not mean kinetic energy; temperature increases sufficient-energy fraction.

decisions.judgement: Catalyst rate/unchanged-overall definition does not prescribe a new catalyst reaction.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Use source-justified rate/catalyst examples linked3.15/3.16.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Peroxide example cross-links3.16; gas acceleration alone cannot prove regenerated identity.

decisions.judgement: Alternative lower-activation-energy pathway is general rather than a named reaction.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Use source-justified rate/catalyst examples linked3.15/3.16.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Catalyst does not change overall endpoints/enthalpy or supply net reaction energy.

decisions.judgement: Profiles with ΔH and activation energy are equation-linked representations, not a fixed reaction.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Exothermic/endothermic supplied profile; catalysed comparison if included.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Measure barrier from reactants, ΔH between endpoints; numerical diagram does not create a prescribed molecular reaction.

decisions.judgement: Named marble-chip/dilute hydrochloric-acid investigation with separate area and acid-concentration changes.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: CaCO3(s)+2HCl(aq)→CaCl2(aq)+H2O(l)+CO2(g).
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: DiluteHCl, comparable carbonate mass/material/temperature; acid excess throughout if claiming same finalCO2. Collection delay/leaks/dissolution limit observations; one equation serves both variable studies.

decisions.judgement: Named catalytic decomposition of aqueous hydrogen peroxide compares different solids.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Solids are varied; MnO2 is a representative, not the only publisher-prescribed catalyst. Matched peroxide/temperature/sample conditions, no-solid control; gas identity and catalyst regeneration distinct.

decisions.judgement: Reversible symbol and two directions are a cross-topic equation skill.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Represent reversible cases3.18 with ⇌.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Reversible arrow does not establish present equilibrium/equal quantities. It does not prescribe a further chemical pair.

decisions.judgement: Source explicitly gives dehydration of hydrated copper(II)sulfate and heating ammonium chloride as reversible examples.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: CuSO4·5H2O(s)⇌CuSO4(s)+5H2O(g) for hot dehydration; cooled hydration with added liquid water is the reverse demonstration under different conditions.
NH4Cl(s)⇌NH3(g)+HCl(g), with reformation of solid in cooler region.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Source SUCH AS names examples to retain, not an exhaustive reversible-reaction universe. Pentahydrate is standard represented hydrate; state of water depends on heating/collection/addition. Blue solution with excesswater is not proof of pure hydrated crystals. Open demos not proof of dynamic equilibrium; never rigidly seal heated gas-producing tube.

decisions.judgement: Closed-system dynamic-equilibrium concept names no additional reaction.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Use representative reversible model with supplied evidence; cross-link3.18 only where conditions appropriate.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Retain reactants/products and maintained conditions; no need for a sealed dangerous demonstration.

decisions.judgement: Equal opposing rates and constant concentrations describe general equilibrium behaviour.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Use representative reversible model with supplied evidence; cross-link3.18 only where conditions appropriate.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Concentrations need not be equal; plateau alone does not prove dynamic mechanism.

decisions.judgement: Catalyst unchanged equilibrium position is a general equilibrium relationship.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Use representative reversible model with supplied evidence; cross-link3.18 only where conditions appropriate.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Compare actual equilibrium at same maintained conditions; faster approach is not changed yield.

decisions.judgement: Temperature and pressure directions require representative given equilibria, not a named industrial synthesis.
requiredOrRepresentativeCases: Representative supplied reversible equation; ammonia, H2/I2/HI and carbonate equilibrium in notes are illustrative, not newly mandated named cases.
decisions.statesConditionsLimits: Heating endothermic/cooling exothermic; fixedT compression fewergas moles, expansion more; equalgas counts and inert addition at fixedV need qualifications. Le Chatelier name not required.
